en.summary: The new DCU series *Lanterns* is filling in crucial gaps after the events of *Superman*. A surprising character arc for Guy Gardner is already showing significant growth.
en.body:
The new DCU, ushered in by **James Gunn** and **Peter Safran**, is steadily expanding its universe, and **HBO**'s **Lanterns** is proving to be a vital piece of that puzzle. Following the foundational events of **Superman** and the animated **Creature Commandos**, the live-action series is now fleshing out the world and its inhabitants, particularly focusing on the complex legacy of the Green Lantern Corps.

The **Lanterns** premiere offered a glimpse into the post-Superman era, and it’s already delivering on its promise to explore the gaps in this burgeoning universe. The series, which premiered on August 16, 2026, is a key component of Chapter One: Gods and Monsters, with its eight-episode run designed to deepen our understanding of the heroes who paved the way for **Superman**’s public arrival. While **Superman** introduced the world to a powerful new metahuman three years before his own cinematic debut, the groundwork was laid by earlier heroes whose stories are now being explored.

## Guy Gardner's Unexpected Turn

One of the most compelling developments in **Lanterns** so far is the evolution of **Guy Gardner**, portrayed by **Nathan Fillion**. The initial impression of Gardner, seen in **Superman**, was that of a craven opportunist, more concerned with his own economic interests and brand identity than with true heroism. He seemed to prioritize personal gain over the greater good, a stark contrast to the ideals of the Green Lantern Corps.

However, **Lanterns** episode six presented a significant shift. When Gardner returns to Rushville, Nebraska, years after the events of episode five, he doesn't arrive with the expected arrogance. Instead, he displays a surprising level of concern for his predecessor, Hal Jordan. This moment indicates a notable character growth, suggesting that the events following **Superman** have indeed impacted Gardner, pushing him towards a more selfless path. It’s a testament to the writing that a character initially perceived as flawed is now showing signs of genuine development.

## Building the DCU Foundation

**Lanterns** is not just about individual character arcs; it's crucial for establishing the present-day landscape of the DCU. By exploring the aftermath of major events and the roles of various heroes, the series provides context for future stories. It confirms that elements from **The Suicide Squad** and **Peacemaker** season one are canon, weaving a connected narrative tapestry. This deliberate world-building is essential for fans who are invested in the long-term vision of **James Gunn** and **Peter Safran**’s DCU.

## What's Next for the Corps

With **Lanterns** continuing its run, fans are eager to see how these character developments will unfold and how they will further shape the DCU. The series, along with other upcoming projects like **Creature Commandos** season two and **The People v. Gorilla Grodd**, is set to fill out the 2027 slate, building anticipation for what’s to come. The careful pacing and deliberate storytelling suggest that **Lanterns** is laying essential groundwork for future heroes and conflicts within this interconnected universe.

content_raw: This article contains spoilers for Lanterns season 1 episode 6 . Guy Gardner isn’t a good guy. He’s not a bad guy by any stretch of the imagination, at least not in a world where Lex Luthor and the White Dragon exist. But anyone who saw Superman knows that the Earth’s current Green Lantern is a craven opportunist, someone who uses the massive power bestowed upon him mostly to advance his own economic interests rather than doing good as its own reward. As played by Nathan Fillion , Guy concerns himself with brand identity and the fate of the Justice Gang more than he does stopping Lex Luthor or the hostile nation of Boravia. So when Guy shows back up in Lanterns , coming to Rushville, Nebraska years after the events of episode five, one would expect him to feel pretty high and mighty. After all, Hal Jordan, heretofore the only human Green Lantern, had completely screwed up, as had the Guaridans’ choice for his replacement, John Stewart. Guy has the opportunity to prove that only he is worthy to wear the ring. Yet, instead, Guy shows something like concern for his predecessor, indicating that some character growth in the world after Superman . Even though it’s preceded by Creature Commandos , which itself indicated that some parts of The Suicide Squad and season one of Peacemaker are canon, Superman was the first proper entry in the new DCU inaugurated by James Gunn and DC Studios co-head Peter Safran. As such, Superman entered a world already inhabited by superheroes, even though his public arrival, three years before the events of that movie, introduced the most powerful meta-human in the world. Through Superman , Creature Commandos , and the second season of Peacemaker , we got a sense of the heroes who preceeded Superman: the members of the Justice League and Task Force X, of course, but also those who show up on the mural in the Hall of Justice, which includes Golden Age characters like Starman and Iron Munro. Lanterns went further to show that Green Lantern had been on Earth since 1986, making Hal Jordan a craggy veteran by the time Superman debuted in Metropolis. While these events have set up the DCU’s past, Lanterns gives us a better sense of the DCU’s present, after the events of Superman. Superman wasn’t just about how the Man of Steel defeated Lex Luthor and saved Jarhanpur from Boravia. It was also about how Superman inspired people with his goodness, including other superheroes. And no hero needed inspiration more than Guy Gardner, the bowl-cut sporting GL in the Justice Gang. When we first meet Guy, he shows little care for civilians or the kaiju that he and the Justice League take down. But by the end of the movie, he and the Justice Gang decide to help the people of Jarhanpur, even if doing so might harm their brand and the profits it can bring.
